subject: Observability and SIEM hookup for private (VPC/on-prem) deployment
body:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: security.team@acme.com
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Observability export options for private deployment

Hi Monica,

We are finalizing the network/security design for our Redwood private deployment in our AWS VPC and need to lock down observability exports. Specifically:
- How do logs (application & access) get to our SIEM — push or pull?
- Metrics (Prometheus) remote_write or agent scrape? TLS requirements?
- Tracing: can we get OTLP traces out to our tracing backend?
- Retention hints, especially for PII-scrubbed logs.

We have a SOC2 audit in May and our security ops team needs a checklist + network/IP/port list to put in our ticketing system.

Can your team share the recommended architecture and any runbook we can attach to the compliance ticket?

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Doe
Director, Cloud Security
Acme Financial

---
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Observability export options for private deployment

Jane — thanks for the clear list. I attached a short architecture diagram and a SIEM checklist (see attachments). High-level options we recommend for private/VPC deployments:

1) Logs: two supported patterns
   - Push (recommended): Redwood forwarder runs inside customer's VPC (sidecar/collector) and ships to your SIEM over mTLS / syslog-ng (CEF) to a private ingestion endpoint. This avoids opening wide inbound access and is easier for air-gapped customers.
   - Pull (allowed): If your SIEM vendor prefers, we can expose a secure pull endpoint behind a private link or VPC peer; requires network rules for Redwood egress and signed tokens.

2) Metrics:
   - Prometheus remote_write from a customer-managed collector to your internal TSDB/Prometheus ingestion. We can also scrape if you permit a scrape endpoint; remote_write is preferred for scale and ACL control. TLS with client certs is supported.

3) Traces:
   - OpenTelemetry (OTLP) exporter from our private control-plane connector to your OTLP/Jaeger/Tempo endpoint. We support batching, TLS, and attribute filtering on the collector to avoid PII.

4) Retention & PII:
   - We recommend inline redaction policies at the collector before shipping. Our collector supports regex-based suppression and field-level masking; retention policy should be defined on your SIEM side for audit needs.

Network/security considerations (summary):
- Outbound-only connections from your VPC to your SIEM/private ingest (mTLS preferred)
- IP ranges and ports: see attached checklist; expect TCP 6514 (syslog TLS), 443 for HTTPS/OTLP-gRPC, 9411/4317 if using alternatives
- Mutual TLS or client cert auth for ingestion endpoints is strongly recommended

I'm looping in Hiro and Evelyn to add the exact port/IP list and SOC2 evidence notes. If the team is open, we suggest a 30-min call early next week to align and deliver a short runbook for your audit.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-observability-priv-deploy-arch.pdf, siem-integration-checklist.xlsx

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>

Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Observability export options for private deployment

Monica / Jane — adding a few low-level networking details for the runbook:

- Egress: Our collectors initiate outbound TLS connections to your ingest endpoints. If you require fixed IPs on the firewall, we can provide a small published egress range scoped to the dedicated deployment.
- PrivateLink vs VPC Peering: PrivateLink is better for SaaS-style private endpoints (no route table changes). VPC peering is acceptable for on-prem/hybrid but increases blast radius for network traffic.
- Ports/protocols: 6514 (syslog over TLS), 443 (OTLP-gRPC/HTTP), 4317 (OTLP gRPC default), 9095 (prometheus push gateway/remote write via HTTPS).
- Authentication: mTLS + token-based rotation. For SIEMs that only accept syslog over TLS, we'll fall back to syslog-ng with TLS and client certs.
- DNS requirements: allow our collector to resolve your private endpoints; if using PrivateLink, provide the endpoint DNS names (we also support listing by IP).
- Message formats: CEF, LEEF or JSON — our forwarder can emit any of these; recommend JSON for structured fields to simplify SIEM parsing.

I'll attach a short runbook snippet for configuring the collector and firewall rules (priv-observability-runbook.md).

- Hiro
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jane — quick compliance checklist items to capture for SOC2:
- Evidence that logs are delivered (ingest acknowledgements, delivery timestamps)
- Proof of redaction rules applied before export (collector configuration + test vectors)
- Access controls for the collector (IAM role, key rotation policies)
- Retention policy documented and implemented on the SIEM side
- TLS/mutual auth config and certificate rotation schedule

We can provide sample export logs and a small test plan you can run to validate redaction prior to audit.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 13:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Observability export options for private deployment

Hi all — attaching a short runbook and a sample OTLP collector config snippet. Quick operational notes:
- Enable batch_size=8192 and max_latency_ms=200 for OTLP to balance throughput/latency when shipping traces out of a private environment.
- Use attribute filters to drop PII: e.g., drop attributes matching /ssn|credit_card|account_number/
- For Prometheus remote_write, set write_relabel_configs to strip labels with PII and use TLS with client cert.

If helpful, we can spin a temporary test endpoint in our staging tenant so your security team can validate ingestion and redaction without touching production.

Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: priv-observability-runbook.md
